overview.text: Orans means praying in Latin. In a report published by the Romanian Patriarchate’s Basilica agency, Patriarch Daniel explains the extended-arm image of the Mother of God as an image of the Church in prayer. It is a type, not a single named object.

sourceRefs.locator: Patriarch Daniel’s explanation of the extended-arm icon

blocks.text: The defining gesture is Mary’s outstretched arms in prayer. The Patriarch’s explanation also addresses a form with Christ depicted on her chest. The Kyiv mosaic reproduced here shows the raised-arm figure without that additional image; the source’s account is therefore broader than this one example.

blocks.text: One named example discussed by the OCA is the Mirozh icon. Its account identifies the praying type, describes Saints Dovmont-Timothy and Martha beside Mary, and records a copy retained at the monastery after the venerated icon was removed. Those Pskov details concern Mirozh and must not be transferred to the Kyiv mosaic.

blocks.text: Patriarch Daniel connects the image with the Church receiving Christ’s blessing and living through it. His remarks were published when the Romanian Holy Synod established the Order of the Praying Theotokos in 2022, providing a modern official explanation of the image’s ecclesial meaning.

images.description: Its height is 6 m. Circa 2 mln of tesserae were used in a mosaic set. It is one biggest monumental examples of Old Rus art. “Orans” in Greek means “praying”. This image is one of the main iconographic types of the portrayal of the Virgin Mary that presents her image with her hands raised in prayer. The Virgin Orans is called “the Unbreakable Wall”. From ancient times it is believed that as long as the image of the Virgin Orans is in St. Sophia so long the city of Kyiv and all Rus stand.
